name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection, definition and evolving strategies of coordinated link sharing and networked manipulation on social media platforms. This is the researcher's signature line, spanning the CooRnet method, cross-electoral case studies and conceptual entries.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation Narratives
description: Mapping mis-, dis- and mal-information within hybrid media systems, including problematic health content, fake-news taxonomies, and monitoring of disinformation narratives around elections, war and public health.

name: Elections & Political Communication
description: Empirical studies of media and social-media dynamics around electoral campaigns — Italian general elections (2018, 2022), European 2019, German 2021, Brazil, and comparative work on partisanship, populism and polarization.

name: Platform Governance, APIs & DSA-Era Research Access
description: Critical analysis of platform policies (Meta's political content reduction, algorithmic curation), the availability of research APIs and tools in the Digital Services Act era, and the methodological consequences of shrinking data access.

name: Generative AI & Media
description: AI-assisted verification, synthetic visual persuasion, LLMs-in-the-loop pipelines for content analysis, and embedding models for political news — reflecting both the vera.ai project legacy and the researcher's new master's course on Generative AI and Media.

name: Computational Social Science & Digital Methods
description: Methodological reflection and toolmaking for social-media data analysis: ethics of big data, R/Python workflows, Facebook ads as sampling frames, and integrating machine learning into communication research.

name: Italian Media Ecosystem (MINE)
description: The institutional umbrella and empirical focus of the MINE programme: mapping Italian news coverage, hyperpartisan networks, insular vs cross-partisan audiences, and the interplay between traditional and digital Italian media.

name: Polarization & Hybrid Media Systems
description: How social and traditional media jointly shape political polarization, partisan attention, and the amplification of extremes — a cross-cutting theme from the 2013 Italian talk-show studies to recent Latin American and comparative work.

name: Social TV & Audience Engagement
description: Second-screen practices, TV-Twitter interactions and algorithmic catalogues (Netflix). A historically important strand of the researcher's work retained for archival cohesion, though less active on the current agenda.

name: Problematic Content in the Global South
description: Studies of coordinated networks circulating problematic health and political content in India, Nigeria and Brazil — extending coordination research beyond Euro-American contexts through the Gates-funded MINE sub-project and follow-ups.

name: Sociocybernetics & Social Systems Theory
description: The researcher's theoretical anchor: Luhmannian systems theory, sociocybernetics, and observation of social systems in the era of big data. Foundational lens informing the wider empirical agenda.

name: Public and Sociotechnical Approaches to AI Safety Evaluation
description: Papers framing AI safety practices—red-teaming and evaluation—as sociotechnical activities requiring public involvement, labor consideration, and participatory science methods rather than purely technical procedures.

name: Online Radicalization and Extremism Across Platforms
description: Empirical and review studies of how extremist actors (far-right, jihadist) exploit platform affordances, algorithms, and multimodal content to spread and normalize radical ideologies online.

name: Retrospective Essays on Platformization and Social Media's Trajectory
description: Reflective anniversary/position essays diagnosing the current state of social media and platform economies, tracing how platformization, political economy, and scam/extractive logics have reshaped online life over the past decade.

name: Public Attitudes and Labor Experiences with AI
description: Survey- and discourse-based studies of how publics and workers perceive, use, and are shaped by AI systems, including stakeholder discourse, national attitudes, and worker-reported productivity and displacement effects.

name: LLMs and Computational Methods for Research Workflows
description: Methodological papers deploying LLMs or fine-tuned models to augment scholarly tasks such as peer review, qualitative coding, and domain-specific classification, with attention to human-in-the-loop design and evaluation.

name: Message-Based Interventions for Climate Communication and Misinformation Resistance
description: Experimental and review studies testing how framed messages, chatbots, or inoculation techniques shape audience attitudes, resistance to misinformation, and engagement with climate or conspiracy content.
